policies.title: Japanese nationals: outside the foreign-visa application scope
policies.summary: Japanese nationals are not foreign visa applicants under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa process.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish the document requirements for a Japanese national's particular route or carrier.
It does not determine the treatment of a non-Japanese passport held by a dual Japanese national.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: 90-day visa exemption
policies.summary: The listed passport nationalities and regions are visa-exempt for a short stay, with a 90-day landing permission in the ordinary case.
conditions: Applies to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs short-stay exemption arrangement; it does not establish work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, or special-document treatment.
The source says landing permission is 90 days for countries and regions other than its listed 15- and 30-day exceptions.
AT, DE, IE, LI, MX, CH, and GB are marked as arrangements permitting stays of up to six months; a traveller wishing to remain beyond 90 days must apply for an extension before expiry.

policies.title: Brunei ordinary passports: 30-day visa exemption
policies.summary: Brunei nationals are visa-exempt for a landing permission of 30 days.
conditions: This is the Ministry of Foreign Affairs short-stay arrangement and does not establish work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, or special-document treatment.

policies.title: Indonesia: registered ICAO ePassport short-stay exemption
policies.summary: Indonesian nationals are visa-exempt for 15 days only with an ICAO-compliant ePassport registered at a Japanese diplomatic mission in Indonesia.
conditions: The ICAO-compliant ePassport must be registered at the Embassy, Consulate-General, or Consulate of Japan in Indonesia.
Registration is valid for three years or until the passport expires, whichever is earlier.
The source does not establish visa-free entry for an Indonesian passport holder who lacks the required ePassport registration.

policies.title: Malaysia: ICAO ePassport short-stay exemption
policies.summary: Malaysian nationals are visa-exempt only when holding an ICAO-compliant ePassport.
conditions: The source says a holder without the required ePassport is advised to obtain a visa in advance and may otherwise be strictly examined and refused entry.
The normal landing-permission period for this arrangement is 90 days.

policies.title: Thailand: ICAO ePassport 15-day visa exemption
policies.summary: Thai nationals are visa-exempt for 15 days only when holding an ICAO-compliant ePassport.
conditions: The source says a holder without the required ePassport is requested to obtain a visa in advance and will otherwise be refused entry.
This policy does not establish work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, or special-document treatment.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: ICAO ePassport 90-day visa exemption
policies.summary: These nationalities are visa-exempt for a normal 90-day short stay only when holding an ICAO-compliant ePassport.
conditions: The ePassport condition took effect for RS on 2011-05-01, AE on 2022-11-01, BR on 2023-09-30, PA on 2024-04-01, PY on 2025-06-01, PE on 2025-07-01, and ME on 2025-09-01.
The source says a holder without the required ePassport is requested to obtain a visa in advance and will otherwise be refused entry.
This policy does not establish work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, or special-document treatment.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: ICAO machine-readable passport visa exemption
policies.summary: Barbados, Lesotho, and Türkiye nationals are visa-exempt for a normal 90-day short stay only with an ICAO-compliant machine-readable passport.
conditions: The machine-readable-passport condition has applied since 2010-04-01 for BB and LS and since 2011-04-01 for TR.
The source says a holder without the required passport is advised to obtain a visa in advance and may otherwise be strictly examined and refused entry.

policies.title: Taiwan: personal-ID-number passport short-stay exemption
policies.summary: The visa exemption for Taiwan is limited to passport holders whose passports contain a personal ID number.
conditions: The source does not establish the exemption for a Taiwan passport without a personal ID number.
The normal landing-permission period for this arrangement is 90 days.

policies.title: Hong Kong: SAR passport or qualifying BN(O) passport visa exemption
policies.summary: Hong Kong citizens are visa-exempt only with a Hong Kong SAR passport or a British National (Overseas) passport with a right of residence in Hong Kong.
conditions: The policy is limited to a Hong Kong SAR passport issued by the Hong Kong SAR of the People's Republic of China, or a BN(O) passport where the holder has the right of residence in Hong Kong.
The normal landing-permission period for this arrangement is 90 days; other British statuses are not established by this ISO-code policy.

policies.title: Macao: SAR passport short-stay exemption
policies.summary: Macao citizens are visa-exempt only with a Macao SAR passport issued by the Macao SAR of the People's Republic of China.
conditions: The source does not establish the exemption for another passport type held by a Macao citizen.
The normal landing-permission period for this arrangement is 90 days.

policies.title: Qatar: registered ICAO ePassport 30-day visa exemption
policies.summary: Qatari nationals are visa-exempt for 30 days only with an ICAO-compliant ePassport registered at a Japanese diplomatic mission.
conditions: The ICAO-compliant ePassport must be registered at the Embassy, Consulate-General, or Consulate of Japan.
Registration is valid for three years or until the passport expires, whichever is earlier.
The source does not establish visa-free entry for a Qatari passport holder who lacks the required registration.

policies.title: Uruguay: recognized ordinary passport short-stay exemption
policies.summary: Uruguayan nationals remain visa-exempt only when using an ordinary passport version recognized by Japan.
conditions: Japan does not recognize the new Uruguayan ordinary passport version issued after 2025-04-16 that omits place of birth on the personal-data page; it is not eligible for travel to Japan.
The exemption remains available to holders of the old passport version, including an old-version passport issued after that date.
The normal landing-permission period for this arrangement is 90 days.

policies.title: Non-visa-exempt ordinary passports: visa required
policies.summary: Ordinary passport holders from these non-visa-exempt nationality codes require a visa for Japan's short-term stay category, subject to the distinct residence-conditioned eVISA route stated below.
conditions: This policy is limited to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs short-term-stay category: up to 90 days for tourism, business, visiting friends or relatives, or similar activities without remuneration.
It does not establish work, long-stay, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, refugee, stateless, or other special-document treatment.

An eVISA is a conditional application route, not a universal passport-nationality entitlement: eligible ordinary-passport travellers must be non-exempt and satisfy the stated residence, purpose, mode-of-travel, and any accredited-agency conditions.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says all non-exempt foreign nationals residing in AU, BR, KH, CA, SA, ZA, TW, GB, or US may use the official eVISA website for tourism; CN residents in CN, PH residents in a qualifying package tour, and VN residents in a qualifying package tour have stated routes; further accredited-agency routes apply to eligible residents in HK, IN, ID, MO, MN, KR except Jeju, SG, and AE.

The eVISA route is for an ordinary-passport, single-entry tourism stay generally up to 90 days and requires air travel or the specified international scheduled ferries. An interview may still be requested.

application.label: JAPAN eVISA official application website
steps: First confirm that the passport holder is not visa-exempt and satisfies the applicable residence-based eVISA route.
Apply online through the official JAPAN eVISA website, or use the accredited-agency route where the Ministry of Foreign Affairs requires it.
For an issued eVISA, display the Visa issuance notice online at departure; a PDF, screenshot, or printed copy is not accepted.

conflicts.explanation: The fallback labels Cambodia evisa, but the official source makes eVISA eligibility depend on residence in Cambodia and other conditions; the passport-level baseline is visa_required with a conditional eVISA route.
The fallback labels Mongolia evisa, but the official source makes the route available to eligible foreign residents in Mongolia through an accredited agency; it is not universal passport eligibility.
The fallback labels Saudi Arabia evisa, but the official source makes eVISA eligibility depend on residence in Saudi Arabia and other conditions; the passport-level baseline is visa_required.
The fallback labels South Africa evisa, but the official source makes eVISA eligibility depend on residence in South Africa and other conditions; the passport-level baseline is visa_required.
